title: OneDrive: pay-as-you-go storage beyond licensed quotas
summary: The briefing agrees with the roadmap and Microsoft's tenant notice, including the rollout window and paused government-cloud release. Microsoft documentation supports the storage controls, licensing prerequisites, published meter and warning that budgets do not stop billing.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a new consumption-based OneDrive storage meter that lets selected accounts exceed licensed storage limits.
claims.quote: New pay-as-you-go, consumption-based meter for additional OneDrive storage. Control which OneDrive accounts can grow beyond their licensed storage limits and give selected users more space as needed.

claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out", "statusKey": "rolling-out"

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: OneDrive Extra Storage capacity packs are a separate option for purchasing additional storage.
claims.quote: If a user needs more OneDrive storage, you can buy OneDrive Extra Storage in the Microsoft 365 admin center. ... OneDrive Extra Storage is sold as capacity packs in 100-GB, 500-GB, and 1-TB through 6-TB sizes.

claims.claim: The cited billing setup documentation does not discuss changes to content-access permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage" preview pricing general availability permissions content access; "OneDrive Storage" "content-access" permissions. Read the full Billing node setup page and Add storage's OneDrive section; neither describes content-access permission changes.

claims.claim: The Region selected during billing setup determines where the tenant ID and usage data are stored.
claims.quote: From the Region drop-down list, select a region. This selection determines where the tenant ID and usage data are stored.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing; controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Budgets apply at billing-policy level, not to individual users or sites.
claims.quote: You can only set budgets at the billing policy level, not for individual users, agents, or sites. This policy means any limits or alerts apply to all services and users under the policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; controls[2].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Reaching a budget's threshold does not stop the service or billing.
claims.quote: Reaching 100% of your budget doesn't stop the service or billing.

claims.claim: The documented way to stop billing is to disconnect the service rather than rely on its budget.
claims.quote: The only way to stop billing is to Disconnect a pay-as-you-go service. Reaching 100% of your budget doesn't stop the service or billing.

claims.claim: Budget alert notifications can take up to 24 hours to arrive.
claims.quote: It can take up to 24 hours for recipients to receive budget alert notifications.

claims.claim: The default budget alert percentage is 100%.
claims.quote: By default, the budget percentage that triggers alerts is 100%.

claims.claim: Administrators can add up to four additional budget alert thresholds.
claims.quote: You can add up to four more thresholds (1-99%).

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Cap; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Additional budget alert thresholds can be set between 1% and 99%.
claims.quote: To set more alerts, select Add more and enter a new value. You can add up to four more thresholds (1-99%).

claims.claim: Consumption data can take up to four hours to appear in the spending graph.
claims.quote: Consumption data can take up to four hours to appear in the graph.

claims.quote: You can also monitor your pay-as-you-go usage and costs in Microsoft Cost Management for Azure. Ensure you have at least read access to the billing resource group.

claims.claim: OneDrive Storage billing policies automatically use All users rather than a selected group.
claims.quote: Choosing users only applies to Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go services. For all other services, the All users option is automatically applied.

claims.claim: A billing policy can be connected in Microsoft 365 admin center at Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Services > Connect a policy > policy > Connection status.
claims.quote: Select the Services tab. ... select Connect a policy. ... find the billing policy that you want to connect to, and then select the Connection status toggle to set it to Connected.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for connecting or disconnecting this OneDrive Storage billing service.
claims.quote: Searched: "OneDrive" "billing policy" "API" "pay-as-you-go"; "Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage" billing policy API PowerShell budget per user spending limit. Read Billing node setup; results document UI connections and Backup-only app billing, not OneDrive Storage connection automation.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second row; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The per-user limit is set in Microsoft 365 admin center at Users > Active users > user > OneDrive > Storage used > Edit > Maximum storage for this user.
claims.quote: Expand Users and select Active users. ... Select the user ... Go to the OneDrive tab. ... Under Storage used, select Edit. ... Choose the Maximum storage for this user option and set the storage limit.

claims.claim: SharePoint Online PowerShell sets the per-user quota with Set-SPOSite -Identity <OneDrive site URL> -StorageQuota <MB> -StorageQuotaWarningLevel <MB>.
claims.quote: Set-SPOSite -Identity $OneDriveSite -StorageQuota $OneDriveStorageQuota -StorageQuotaWarningLevel $OneDriveStorageQuotaWarningLevel

claims.claim: Policy spending alert thresholds are configured in Microsoft 365 admin center at Billing > Pay-as-you-go > policy > Budget > Settings > Send email alerts > Add more.
claims.quote: Select the policy that you want to manage. ... select the Budget tab. ... select Settings. ... Under Send email alerts ... To set more alerts, select Add more and enter a new value.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: third row and API absence paragraph
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API to create or configure this service's billing-policy budgets and alerts.
claims.quote: Searched: "OneDrive Storage" "budget" "PowerShell"; "Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage" billing policy API PowerShell budget per user spending limit. Read Billing node setup and Create a budget; no API for these Microsoft 365 policy budgets was found.

claims.claim: The existing tenant default is set in SharePoint admin center at Settings > Storage limit > Default storage limit.
claims.quote: Go to Settings in the new SharePoint admin center ... Select the OneDrive Storage limit setting. ... In the Default storage limit box, enter the default storage amount (in GB)

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls: fourth row and default-limit paragraph
claims.claim: SharePoint Online PowerShell sets the existing tenant default with Set-SPOTenant -OneDriveStorageQuota <quota>.
claims.quote: Set-SPOTenant -OneDriveStorageQuota <quota>

claims.claim: The tenant-default documentation says a default quota above a user's license allowance is rounded down to that license maximum.
claims.quote: If you specify a value greater than that allowed by a given user's license, that user's storage space is rounded down to the maximum value allowed by their license.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls: default-limit paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed whether enabling OneDrive Storage changes the tenant default's license-based rounding behavior.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage" "OneDriveStorageQuota" default. Read Set the default storage space and Add storage's OneDrive section; the former states license rounding without a pay-as-you-go exception, and the latter documents individual user limits only.

claims.claim: The per-user storage limit is the only documented account-selection switch for exceeding licensed OneDrive quotas with this service.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage" "OneDriveStorageQuota" default; "OneDrive" "billing policy" "API" "pay-as-you-go". Read Add storage, Change user storage, default storage and Billing node setup; no alternative account-selection switch found.

claims.claim: Billing policy creation starts in Microsoft 365 admin center at Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Billing policies > Add a billing policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center, and then go to Billing > Pay-as-you-go. On the Billing policies tab, select Add a billing policy.

claims.claim: The OneDrive Storage setup instructions say to choose Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage in Step 4.
claims.quote: When you reach "Step 4. Review and create the billing policy," select the Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage service.

claims.claim: A user's OneDrive storage can be reviewed in Microsoft 365 admin center at Users > Active users > user > OneDrive > Storage used.
claims.quote: In the left pane, select Users, and then select Active users. Select the user. Select the OneDrive tab. Next to "Storage used," look at the max value

claims.claim: Lowering a storage limit below current usage can affect the user's ability to use OneDrive.
claims.quote: If you decrease the storage limit and a user is over the new limit, their OneDrive will become read-only.

claims.where: Governance controls: API absence paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has not documented an API to create OneDrive Storage billing policies.
claims.quote: Searched: "OneDrive" "billing policy" "API" "pay-as-you-go"; "Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage" billing policy API PowerShell budget per user spending limit. Read Billing node setup and Backup billing search excerpts; the latter's app policy operation is explicitly Backup-specific.

claims.claim: A service is disconnected by turning off its Connection status toggle.
claims.quote: In the Connection status column, select the Connected toggle to turn it off.

claims.claim: The separate budget article gives Copilot > Billing & usage, whereas this service's Billing node article gives Billing > Pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Billing & usage.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises reviewing billing and usage after disconnecting the service.
claims.quote: After you disconnect the service, review your billing and usage to ensure no further charges are applied.
